To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for any class of “nice functions”, there is a “difficult” distribution; (ii) for any distribution, there is a class of “difficult functions”; (iii) for any function and distribution, there are some “nice” parameters.

1) for any class of “nice target functions”, there are distributions which make the corresponding learning problem hard, 2) for any class distribution which makes a learning problem hard, there are “nicely behaving target functions” for which learning is still hard, and 3) there are simple target functions, and simple distributions, for which learning is hard.
(a) for a large class of “nice target functions”, there are “difficult” input distributions, and (b) for a large family of “difficult target functions”, there exist “simple” input distributions.
